question: Which items need restocking right now, and how urgent is each one?
Explain why the 1.5L K15C DualJet Engine at WH-GUR needs restocking.
When is the 12V 60Ah Exide Battery at WH-KOL predicted to run out of stock?
What is the average daily consumption for the Front Ventilated Disc Brake Pad at WH-GUR?
What is the average daily consumption for a given part and warehouse?
Explain why a given part at a given warehouse needs restocking.
When is a given part at a given warehouse predicted to run out of stock?
Does a given part at a given warehouse genuinely need restocking, or could it be a false positive?
Which items need restocking right now, and how urgent is each one?
sql: WITH latest_snapshot AS (  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY PART_KEY, WAREHOUSE_KEY ORDER BY SNAPSHOT_DATE_KEY DESC) AS rn  FROM gold_dev.supply_chain_analytics.fact_inventory_snapshot)SELECT  dp.PART_ID,  dp.PART_NAME,  dw.WAREHOUSE_ID,  ls.QUANTITY_ON_HAND AS current_stock_qty,  ls.SAFETY_STOCK_QTY AS reorder_point_qty,  ROUND(ab_training.agentic_restock.avg_daily_consumption(dp.PART_ID, dw.WAREHOUSE_ID, 14), 2) AS avg_daily_consumption,  ab_training.agentic_restock.predicted_stockout_date(dp.PART_ID, dw.WAREHOUSE_ID) AS predicted_stockout_date,  ab_training.agentic_restock.classify_urgency(    ls.STOCKOUT_RISK,    datediff(ab_training.agentic_restock.predicted_stockout_date(dp.PART_ID, dw.WAREHOUSE_ID), current_date())  ) AS urgency_level,  ab_training.agentic_restock.requested_restock_qty(dp.PART_ID, dw.WAREHOUSE_ID) AS requested_restock_qtyFROM latest_snapshot lsJOIN gold_dev.dim.dim_part dp ON ls.PART_KEY = dp.PART_KEY AND dp.IS_CURRENT = trueJOIN gold_dev.dim.dim_warehouse dw ON ls.WAREHOUSE_KEY = dw.WAREHOUSE_KEYWHERE ls.rn = 1 AND dp.LIFECYCLE_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND dw.OPERATIONAL_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND ls.QUANTITY_ON_HAND <= ls.SAFETY_STOCK_QTYORDER BY urgency_level, dp.PART_ID

content: Urgency levels (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), stockout forecasts, average daily consumption, suggested reorder quantities, supplier lead time, and the restock veto decision are all computed by Unity Catalog functions in ab_training.agentic_restock (avg_daily_consumption, predicted_stockout_date, classify_urgency, requested_restock_qty, needs_restock, restock_candidate_summary, avg_lead_time_days). Always call these functions instead of recomputing this logic with ad-hoc SQL -- they are the governed source of truth also used by the Lakeflow trigger job and the Supervisor Agent.The real inventory/consumption/procurement/restock-request data lives in Data Engineering's gold_dev star schema, NOT in ab_training.agentic_restock: gold_dev.supply_chain_analytics.fact_inventory_snapshot (daily stock snapshot; QUANTITY_ON_HAND, SAFETY_STOCK_QTY = reorder trigger, MAX_STOCK_LEVEL = restock target, STOCKOUT_RISK), fact_inventory_transaction (ISSUE/RECEIPT/TRANSFER movements; ISSUE rows are consumption), fact_procurement (purchase orders), and fact_restock_request (one row per requested part-line per quote, joined to gold_dev.dim.dim_request_status for status/urgency/decision). Parts and warehouses are gold_dev.dim.dim_part and dim_warehouse, joined to the facts on PART_KEY/WAREHOUSE_KEY surrogate keys but identified externally by PART_ID/WAREHOUSE_ID business keys.fact_inventory_snapshot is a daily snapshot (one row per part x warehouse x day), not a single current-state row -- always take the row with the MAX(SNAPSHOT_DATE_KEY) per part/warehouse (e.g. via MAX_BY or a ROW_NUMBER() window), never assume there's exactly one row.A restock candidate is any part/warehouse whose latest fact_inventory_snapshot row has QUANTITY_ON_HAND <= SAFETY_STOCK_QTY, restricted to dim_part.LIFECYCLE_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' and dim_warehouse.OPERATIONAL_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'. quote_metadata (in ab_training.agentic_restock) holds Teams/Review-App fields (summary_report, teams_message_id, databricks_preview_url, decision_comments) for each quote_id -- join it to fact_restock_request.QUOTE_ID for the full quote picture; it does not duplicate status/urgency, which always comes fresh from dim_request_status.
